children: Boston Consulting Group (BCG) has announced the expansion of its Riyadh office, adding space and headcount to serve growing client demand across Saudi Arabia.
The expansion is a visible expression of BCG's long-term commitment to the kingdom, where the firm has served clients since 2008 and opened its first Riyadh office in 2015.

What began in 2008 has since grown into a team of more than 350 consultants who have delivered over 2,000 projects across the sectors central to the kingdom’s transformation and, in 2026, an expanded office to support Saudi Arabia’s next phase of growth. Saudi Arabia remains a long-term priority market for BCG. As the market evolves, including changes in the pace and mix of government spending, the firm is adapting responsibly while continuing to invest in Saudi talent, local capabilities, and its presence in the kingdom.

The expanded office significantly increases BCG’s footprint in Riyadh, adding capacity for the firm’s growing team alongside new collaboration spaces designed around how consultants and teams now work together. It combines AI-enabled meeting and working environments, sustainability features in line with the firm’s environmental commitments, and design elements that draw on Saudi culture and the character of Riyadh, creating a workplace built to support new ways of working and BCG’s next phase of growth in the kingdom.

BCG's business is integrated across the sectors and institutions driving Vision 2030. The firm serves public institutions, national programmes, portfolio companies, and private-sector organisations, combining deep knowledge of the Saudi context with relevant experience from BCG's global network. Its work spans public-sector transformation, financial services, energy, real estate, advanced manufacturing, supply-chain resilience, healthcare, technology, tourism, entertainment, and human-capital development. Public-sector work is an important part of the Saudi business, and it sits within a client base broad enough to give BCG a resilient platform in the Kingdom.

“Saudi Arabia’s transformation is Saudi-led, and our role is to support those driving it,” said Philippe Cornette de Saint Cyr, Managing Director and Senior Partner, and Head of BCG’s Riyadh Office. “Our expansion reflects our clients’ evolving needs and our long-term commitment to the kingdom, working alongside Saudi professionals to build lasting capabilities aligned with Vision 2030.”

The expansion strengthens BCG's ability to help clients move from strategy to implementation. The firm brings together strategic clarity, applied AI through BCG X and BCG Platinion, and deep sector expertise to deliver measurable improvements in productivity, cost, service quality, resilience, and competitive advantage.

These are the capabilities BCG is now scaling in Riyadh — pairing strategy with hands-on implementation and building domain-specific AI solutions directly within client environments. Saudi colleagues are embedded throughout AI and digital delivery so that solutions fit the local context and knowledge remains within client organisations.

“Our ambition is to remain the leading strategic partner to institutions and businesses in Saudi Arabia,” said Pablo Martinez, Managing Director and Senior Partner, and Head of BCG Middle East. “That means a continued focus on delivering Vision 2030, deeper private-sector engagement, greater emphasis on implementation and measurable impact, and continued investment in AI and digital capabilities. We combine more than 60 years of strategic expertise with applied AI, and our teams advising clients on AI transformation are putting it to work in their own delivery every day.”
Developing Saudi talent is central to BCG's long-term commitment. The firm continues to recruit, mentor, and promote Saudi professionals across consulting, business services, and leadership roles.

Jeel Tamooh, now in its eighth year, brings Saudi students, recent graduates, and early-career professionals into real business challenges paired with BCG mentors, and many alumni now hold senior roles across Saudi companies, government agencies, and investment funds, while others have gone on to build strong careers within BCG in Riyadh. Saudi women lead client transformations and shape strategy in consulting, project-leadership, and client-facing roles across the business.

Beyond individual engagements, BCG contributes to how the market thinks about transformation through published research, roundtables, events, and advisory work. The expanded Riyadh office gives the firm a stronger platform to raise the quality of decision-making across the market and to support the kingdom's next phase of development.
